Nobody runs a sub-3-hour marathon in week one.

And nobody builds an impressive marketing engine from scratch in month one (despite what your CEO hopes for).

I keep noticing how similar these two jobs are.

When you start marathon training, you don't have a base. You have legs, ambition, and a Strava account that's mostly empty. 

The new head of marketing walks in with the same thing: no pipeline, no attribution, and a CEO who wanted results yesterday.

Here's what both have taught me:

☝🏻 Base miles are boring. Do them anyway.

Easy runs build the engine. Positioning, ICP, and tracking build the marketing engine. Nobody claps for either.

✌🏻You can't sprint every day.

Run hard every day and you get hurt. Launch a new channel every week and nothing gets enough time (nor budget) to work.

🤟🏻 The long run is the whole point.

SEO, content, brand. Those are the 20+ milers of marketing. They feel slow until the day they carry you.

Your finish time is just the receipt of all the work you’ve been doing. So was your Q4 pipeline, sorry.

My marathon PR is 3:53. My goal is 2:55.

That gap doesn't close with one heroic workout. It closes with hundreds of quiet, unsexy ones.

Same with marketing.

Build the base, strengthen the base.

The speed shows up later.

📏 Add continuous level to your magnetic level indicator without shutting down the process.

In sugarcane processing, the steam boiler sits at the heart of the facility. It drives the cane mills, the evaporators, the clarifiers and sometimes electrical generators. Some of these mills date back 100 years or more, and level control in the boiler is critical for safety, efficiency and profitability.

A sugar mill controlled water level in its steam drum with three differential pressure transmitters in two of three voting logic. The team wanted a second continuous level technology to serve as a redundancy to the DP cells, one they could integrate into the control system. The mill already had an SOR 1100 Series Magnetic Level Indicator installed as a redundant visual indicator to the sight glass required by boiler code.

SOR proposed the new SOR Measurement and Control 1310 Magnetostrictive Level Transmitter. The SOR 1310 uses the magnetic field from the float already inside the MLI to determine process level and outputs a 4-20 mA signal.

Installation took two people.

🔩 Mount the transmitter flush to the side of the MLI with two stainless steel hose clamps
🧱 Add an insulation pad to protect the transmitter from the 210°F process temperature
🔌 Make a two-wire hookup to the dual compartment housing on the transmitter head
🚫 Close no valves and shut down no process

The SOR 1310 started reading level as soon as it was wired. The control room set up the signal for operations to display. SOR asked the mill to trend the SOR 1310 against its DP cells. Over one week, both trend lines coincided, which showed the transmitter tracked boiler level correctly.

What the SOR 1310 brings to your level loop:
🎯 ±0.032 inch (±0.813 mm) accuracy, with measurement ranges up to 20 feet (6.1 m)
🔀 Top level and interface level measurement
📡 4-20 mA analog output with HART digital output
🔧 Quick-Cal function for simple recalibration
🖥️ Local LCD display
🧰 Non-ferrous mounts for easy installation or removal on an MLI, with direct insertion available for various tank applications
🛡️ Two year warranty

Think about the vessel where one level reading is not enough. A second continuous technology, installed without a shutdown, gives you a cross-check against your current loop.
